title: Pivot Lane deploy pocket guide + 72hr calendar (Mar 2026) - WIP
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-focused runbook for the "pivot lane" mini-rollout pattern — intended for small binary flips or service-level config changes that need a tight 72-hour watch window. Use this as the day-of checklist, the 72hr calendar for staffing/telemetry, and a shallow release-notes draft to post after the window closes.

Scope and when to use:
- Use for low-to-medium risk changes that touch routing, model variant toggles, autoscale policies, or runtime knobs.
- Not for schema migrations, DB migrations, or multi-region infrastructure changes.
- Target impact: <10% traffic shift per cohort, can be throttled back to 0 quickly.

Quick start checklist (operators):
[ ] Announce start in #deploy-lane 10m before (include link to PR + brief risk summary)
[ ] Confirm smoke tests pass on staging (smoke-id: pivot-smoke-03)
[ ] Verify canary traffic gating rule applied (route=cohort-A, rate=5%)
[ ] Confirm autoscaler policies and reserved capacity look sane (dash: Dedicated-Throughput)
[ ] Start continuous log sampling (obs run: pivot-lane-sample)
[ ] Enable slow-path tracing for affected services (trace-level: high, TTL: 72h)
[ ] Take snapshot of baseline latency/p95/cost metrics and save as artifact
[ ] Notify Customer Success point-of-contact and on-call SRE

72hr calendar (high level):
Day 0 (T0: deploy):
- T-10m: final go/no-go sync in #deploy-lane (PM + release lead + SRE + infra)
- T0: merge + apply route flip to cohort-A (5% traffic)
- T0+15m: run quick smoke + basic queries (happy-path tests)
- T0+30m: if stable, bump cohort-A -> 10%; else, rollback to 0 and escalate
- T0+1h: snapshot telemetry, update release notes draft with first-minute observations

Day 1 (T0+24h):
- 08:00 UTC: health check and latency audit (owner: SRE-1)
- 12:00 UTC: manual review of error rates and model output drift (owner: ML-ops)
- 16:00 UTC: optional bump to cohort-B (up to 30%) if all gates green
- 20:00 UTC: lightweight retro log (what happened day-1) posted to thread

Day 2 (T0+48-72h):
- Continuous monitoring; decide whether to fully roll, hold, or rollback by T0+72h
- T0+72h: final decision sync (release lead + PM + SRE). If green: finalize release notes and promote change to stable routing. If issues: run rollback procedure and start postmortem template.

Rollout decision matrix (quick):
- Green: no user-facing errors, latency delta p95 <= +10%, no regressions in quality evals -> scale up
- Amber: transient errors, intermittent increased latency, or minor quality regression -> pause, investigate, keep at reduced cohort
- Red: sustained error increase, severe latency, or model hallucination spike -> immediate rollback, page on-call SRE & ML-ops

Rollback cheat-sheet:
- Immediate action: set routing back to baseline (route config: stable), disable variant A
- Ingress safeguard: enable throttle 0.1 for affected paths if routing revert delayed
- Communication: post rollback note in thread, @oncall, update linked Jira ticket with steps taken
- Post-rollback checks: verify consumer tiers, run smoke tests, confirm backfill of KV caches if needed

Monitoring & telemetry anchor points:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 across model servers (dash: latency-pulse)
- Errors: 5xx rate and service-specific error signatures (dash: error-hunt)
- Cost: token-per-req and GPU utilization by pool (dash: cost-watch)
- Output quality: run 50-sample evals against baseline prompts (eval job: pivot-drift-50)
- Traces: selective slow-path traces for API call paths and cache misses

Communications plan (who says what):
- Release lead -> #deploy-lane: T0 announce + link to notes (format: short TL;DR + recovery plan)
- SRE -> #ops-incident if amber/red: short signal + pager escalation
- PM -> customer slack / CS if user-facing (template included at bottom)

Release notes draft (shallow, to publish after T0+72h if green):
Title: Pivot Lane: small routing and runtime tweak (Mar 2026)
Summary: A controlled rollout that updated routing for model variant A and adjusted autoscaler smoothing. No user-facing changes expected.
What changed: Updated route mapping for small cohort; adjusted autoscaler target from 60% -> 55% to reduce oscillation.
Why: Reduce latency spikes during short-burst traffic patterns and validate model variant in production.
Rollout cadence: 5% -> 10% -> 30% -> final promote across 72 hours.
Known issues: None observed during the watch window. (If any, we list here with mitigation)
Follow-ups: Evaluate cost delta at T+7 days, and run extended quality eval set.

Checklist for final signoff:
[ ] All monitoring gates green for 72h
[ ] No unresolved user reports or CS tickets related to this change
[ ] Post-change performance baseline saved and linked
[ ] Release notes posted and shared with stakeholders
[ ] Tick the confluence deploy log and close associated JIRA tasks

Open questions / things to decide (TODO):
- Should we pre-warm KV caches for the variant before bumping beyond 10%? Pros: fewer cold-start artefacts. Cons: extra cost during small cohort test. (owner: ML-ops)
- Do we enable GPU quantization fallback in Dedicated pools for this rollout? (owner: infra)
- Do we want an automated canary rollback on p95 > baseline+15% for 15 consecutive minutes? (owner: release-engineering)

Postmortem / retro prompts (if things go wrong):
- Timeline: minute-by-minute notes starting at T0
- Short narratives from each owner (SRE, infra, ML, PM)
- Root cause candidate(s) and immediate fixes applied
- Longer term action items and owners with ETA

Notes-to-self / operator hints:
- If logs show a specific model server node spiking, isolate node and route away before full rollback — sometimes a single node badness looks like rollout fallout
- Keep a local copy of the old route config JSON; it saves 5-10 minutes when rollback is throttled by infra console slowness
- If quality drift is subtle, run the extended prompt set (200 prompts) and look for changes in hallucination rate, not just token-level metrics

Draft of short broadcast template for CS (copy/paste):
Subject: Quick note: small routing update (Mar 2026)
Body: We're running a small, controlled update to routing for variant testing over the next 72 hours. You shouldn't see interruptions; we'll notify if anything impacts customers. Contact: [oncall link]

Appendix: useful links and artifacts
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987
- Smoke job: ci/pivot-smoke-03
- Confluence midline: https://confluence.redwood.ai/deploy-playbooks#pivot-lane
- JIRA: RELE-1428 (deploy), RELE-1430 (monitoring)

End notes: This is a working artifact. Fill in the day-of observations live (timestamp + 1-line note) and we can recycle this into a longer ‘post-deploy’ template for similar minilaunches.

-- Marcus
(Release lead / eng-release-engineering)
